title: Event Table Management System — Cursor Implementation Plan

cursor_execution_instructions: Read this file, SPECIFICATION.md, README.md and repository instructions before editing. Inspect actual files; do not assume specifications are implemented.
Work through tasks in dependency order. Implement each vertical slice including migrations, services, views, templates and meaningful tests before marking it complete.

Preserve the specified Django, HTML, CSS, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, MailDev and SendGrid architecture. Use focused vanilla JavaScript and SVG for the editor; do not replace the application with a SPA.
Use shared domain services for every mutation, including Django admin and background tasks. Never allow direct admin editing to bypass seat, ticket, tenant or audit invariants.

Track status and concrete validation evidence in IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.json. Record blocked checks separately from passes. Do not mark mocked integration tests as real provider or deployment validation.

Complete local implementation and reversible verification autonomously. Do not deploy, send real guest emails, publish registry images or destroy live data merely because deployment commands are listed.
Use synthetic example.test email data for local and automated tests. Real provider checks require a configured staging sender and explicitly selected test recipients.
Do not stop after scaffolding, static UI mockups or TODO handlers. Every completed feature must persist and work end to end.
If external credentials or Docker access are unavailable, continue independent implementation, document the exact blocked verification and never invent successful results.
Resolve and lock compatible dependencies during implementation, using official documentation for version-sensitive APIs.
Update README.md when commands or architecture change. Finish with completed tasks, remaining blockers, actual test results and the startup procedure.

required: Multi-organization event CRUD and scoped roles
Event details, address, logo, dates and timezone
CSV email and ticket-count import with preview
Guest email campaigns and durable delivery
Printable seating plans, rosters and cards
Guest seating links and per-ticket check-in
Security, monitoring, backup and production hardening

architecture.frontend: Django templates, semantic HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript modules and SVG
architecture.jobs: Celery 5.6, one beat instance, PostgreSQL job/outbox state

email.production: SendGrid SMTP with STARTTLS on 587, username apikey, secret-mounted API key

architecture.production: Single Linux host, Docker Compose, Gunicorn and Caddy
architecture.testing: pytest/pytest-django with PostgreSQL; browser automation for real workflows and accessibility; PDF render verification

decisions.decision: Create one stable Ticket UUID per seat entitlement; one Booking per event and normalized email. Never use email as a single-person identity.
Do not enable attendee_names CSV column in version 1. Provide post-import individual attendee editing; reject unsupported columns with a useful message.
Replace total entitlement by default. Never add silently. Duplicate-in-file reject by default; optional aggregate and additive modes require explicit preview.
Derive capacity from active usable seat records. Initial table count/default chairs are creation inputs, not authoritative capacity fields.

Maintain event roster_revision and layout_revision. Seating mutations increment layout_revision; ticket entitlement changes increment roster_revision and layout_revision when seating/publication data changes.

Begin with an Event row lock as the consistent outer lock for all event mutations, then tables, seats, tickets and holds in deterministic order. This serializes writes safely; optimize only if benchmarks require it without weakening invariants.

Unique organization + operation + idempotency key; store request digest and response. Reuse with different payload returns 409. Acquire and complete the record in the same transaction as the mutation.
Use immutable serialized snapshots for guest views and exports; ticket validity and token revocation are checked against live records.
Reference a non-null immutable campaign audience/snapshot record so logical send uniqueness remains enforced even for campaigns that have no layout publication.
SMTP acceptance means submitted, not delivered. Ambiguous acceptance requires reconciliation or explicit resend; never promise exactly-once SMTP delivery.
Use revocable opaque per-ticket QR tokens separate from booking-view tokens. No personally identifying QR payload.
Choose and lock a maintained HTML-to-PDF engine, verify SVG support and install its system libraries in Docker. Deny arbitrary network/local-file fetching.

invariants: One current occupancy per seat and at most one current seat per ticket.
SeatOccupancy contains exactly one of ticket_id or hold_id.
Every related object belongs to the same event and organization.
Blocked/retired seats and cancelled tickets cannot be assigned.
Occupied furniture and seated/checked-in tickets cannot be silently removed.
Whole-table holds cover chairs added while the hold remains active.
Expired holds can be released during the assignment transaction even when beat is stopped.
Guests, exports, job status and APIs enforce object scope; UUID secrecy is not authorization.
Draft edits do not change published snapshots.
Email intent and job progress survive broker loss through PostgreSQL records.
All successful mutations record actor, reason where required, revision and audit details.

tasks.title: Verify scaffold and establish reproducible development environment
implementation_steps: Inspect current configuration and run Compose config validation.
Add locked runtime/test dependencies and test settings using PostgreSQL.
Build and boot dev services when Docker is available; run migrate, check and readiness smoke tests.
Create status tracking with task IDs and evidence; keep missing runtime access visible.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout has documented reproducible startup.
Django checks and health tests pass against PostgreSQL/Redis, or environmental blockers are explicitly recorded.

tasks.title: Authentication, organization isolation and staff roles
implementation_steps: Decide custom User before first application migrations; avoid resetting existing databases.
Implement Organization, Membership and explicit EventGrant permissions.
Add session login/logout/password reset and organization selection.
Enforce organization/event access centrally and require MFA for privileged production roles.
Add throttling and scoped queryset helpers; test guessed UUIDs and role escalation.
acceptance_criteria: Every role matches the specification permission matrix.
Cross-tenant access is denied even with known object IDs.
Privileged production login cannot bypass MFA.

tasks.title: Audited transactional mutation infrastructure
implementation_steps: Implement append-only audit events with PII-safe payloads and request IDs.
Implement idempotency records with unique keys and request hashes.
Define consistent HTTP validation/conflict errors and transaction/lock helpers.
Set a global lock acquisition order and ensure background/admin writes use it.
acceptance_criteria: Failed transactions leave no successful audit/mutation records.
Same idempotency key and payload returns original outcome; changed payload returns 409.
Audit access is organization-scoped and unauthorized mutation is prevented.

tasks.title: Event CRUD and lifecycle
implementation_steps: Implement all event metadata, timezone/date validation and creation defaults.
Add list/search/filter, create/edit/detail and archive/reopen/cancel actions.
Implement lifecycle guards and cancellation hooks for future scheduled campaigns.
Implement safe logo upload decode/re-encode with type/dimension/size limits.
Add responsive HTML/CSS shell, navigation and role-aware actions.
acceptance_criteria: Event details persist correctly and timezone/DST cases are tested.
Archive is reversible; destructive deletion is not ordinary CRUD.
Unsafe logo uploads are rejected.

tasks.title: Room, tables, chairs and geometry services
implementation_steps: Implement Room, RoomObstacle, EventTable and Seat with stable UUIDs and label uniqueness.
Implement table/chair creation, bulk generation, duplication, retirement and derived capacity.
Represent chair coordinates relative to table center; validate finite numeric values, positive dimensions and polygons.
Validate transformed table/chair footprints inside room and overlap; distinguish hard errors from overrideable clearance warnings.
Protect active occupancies through shared mutation hooks used by T08.
acceptance_criteria: 10 tables with 8 chairs yields 80 seats; adding 2 yields 82.
Moving/rotating or renaming preserves seat identity.
Invalid or overlapping geometry is rejected and safe clearance overrides are audited.

tasks.title: Bookings, tickets and quantity reconciliation
implementation_steps: Implement Booking uniqueness by event + normalized email, retaining original email.
Implement stable Ticket UUIDs and never-reused per-booking sequence allocation.
Implement entitlement increases/decreases, cancellation and individual attendee editing.
Remove eligible unassigned/unchecked-in tickets first; require explicit resolution of protected tickets.
Add searchable party and per-ticket list views.
acceptance_criteria: A four-ticket booking creates four independent tickets.
Ticket reductions cannot silently remove occupied or checked-in tickets.
Existing ticket identities remain stable when quantity or names change.

tasks.title: CSV upload, preview and transactional commit
implementation_steps: Implement ImportBatch/ImportRow and private input storage; enforce 5 MB, 10000 rows and configured quantity limits.
Parse UTF-8/BOM, quoted CSV and CRLF; require email and ticket_count.
Implement default duplicate rejection, explicit aggregation/additive modes and default replace-total mode.
Persist preview changes/errors and roster revision; commit with idempotency and locked revalidation.
Implement deliberate valid-row subset and separate replace-roster preview flows; reject silent partial imports.
Add digest replay handling and downloadable sanitized error report.
acceptance_criteria: Reimporting the default file does not double quantities.
Invalid default batches create no partial changes.
Roster changes after preview yield conflict instead of stale commit.
Absence from ordinary import does not delete an existing booking.

tasks.title: Reservation and assignment transaction engine
implementation_steps: Implement Hold and SeatOccupancy with unique seat, unique nullable ticket and XOR database constraints.
Implement seat/multi-seat/whole-table hold, expiry, release, assign, unassign, group assign and swap.
Use outer event lock and deterministic row locks for all related furniture, ticket and hold mutations.
Make chair creation inherit active table hold; retire/shrink workflows fail with impact report unless explicit resolution supplied.
Consume expired holds under lock; implement booking-specific holds and reason-required override policy.
Increment revisions and audit all changes; catch uniqueness failures as conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent same-seat and same-ticket requests cannot create duplicate assignments.
Table hold races with new chairs/assignment preserve coverage.
Atomic swaps roll back completely on failure.
Blocked/retired/cross-event assignments fail.

tasks.title: Layout API and accessible seating forms
implementation_steps: Implement geometry GET/PATCH and expected-version conflicts.
Add list-based assignment, group-preview, hold/release and atomic swap forms.
Provide unassigned search, selected-table inspector data and revision polling.
Return safe error objects with current version and changed objects; keep server validation authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: Stale writes return HTTP 409 without losing other edits.
All graphical actions have usable form/list equivalents.
Unauthorized users cannot mutate through JSON endpoints.

tasks.title: Interactive SVG room and seating editor
implementation_steps: Implement canvas, palette, legend, inspector and searchable unassigned sidebar.
Add pan/zoom, snap, fit, rotation, alignment, multi-select and keyboard movement.
Support ticket-to-chair and party-to-table drag/drop with exact assignment preview.
Implement command-based undo/redo through validated versioned server operations.
Handle conflicts with refresh/reapply UI; never silently overwrite.
Use zoom detail reduction and incremental rendering for large rooms.
acceptance_criteria: Real interactions persist after refresh.
Moving tables moves their chairs without changing assignments.
Keyboard user can create/select/assign/unassign.
Status is understandable without color alone.

tasks.title: Immutable publications and event duplication
implementation_steps: Create immutable versioned geometry/seat/assignment snapshots in one locked transaction.
Validate capacity, room geometry and acknowledged unassigned tickets before publishing.
Keep draft changes separate and compute affected-booking diffs between publications.
Flag republish required after relevant cancellation; live ticket checks override stale snapshot access.
Implement event duplication with metadata/geometry only and new object UUIDs.
acceptance_criteria: Old publications remain unchanged after later edits.
Publishing never sends emails implicitly.
Changed-seat recipients can be derived accurately.

tasks.title: Guest seating access and ticket check-in
implementation_steps: Create high-entropy hashed, expiring/revocable booking-view and per-ticket QR tokens with separate purposes.
Expose only the booking's published details and recheck live ticket validity.
Implement mobile ticket lookup, QR check-in, partial-party arrivals and reasoned undo.
Prevent URL/token leakage through logs and referrers; throttle token endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Guest token cannot access another booking or staff data.
Repeated scan is idempotent and cancelled tickets fail.
Two of four party tickets may check in independently.

tasks.title: Campaign drafts, previews and durable mail outbox
implementation_steps: Implement versioned HTML/plain-text templates for invitation, seating, changes, reminders and cancellations.
Snapshot recipient audience and publication; implement preview, test, send/schedule and cancellation actions.
Store unique logical EmailDelivery records and attempt history in PostgreSQL.
Dispatch after commit plus periodic pending-row scan; claim rows safely and recheck cancellations/suppression.
Implement bounded transient retry, rate limits and explicit ambiguous-acceptance state.
Correlate SendGrid events using non-PII delivery UUID metadata; keep one recipient per message.
acceptance_criteria: MailDev captures expected content and exactly one recipient per logical delivery.
SMTP submitted is not marked delivered.
Redis loss cannot erase queued business intent.
Ambiguous acceptance does not trigger blind duplicate send.

tasks.title: SendGrid delivery webhooks and suppression
implementation_steps: Verify raw-body signatures using the documented SendGrid algorithm/library and configured public key.
Apply bounded timestamp tolerance, event deduplication and idempotent receipt storage.
Handle out-of-order delivery/bounce/complaint events without inappropriate state regression.
Implement suppression and restricted explicit retry/reconciliation actions.
Add narrow CSRF exemption only on the signed webhook route; configure staging delivery test.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid signatures, stale replays and malformed payloads cannot change delivery state.
Duplicate events have one effect.
Suppressed recipients are excluded from later sends.
Real-provider integration result is recorded separately from mocked tests.

tasks.title: Printing, PDF and CSV export
implementation_steps: Implement room plans, table/alphabetical rosters, table/place cards, seating slips and operational reports.
Support A4/A3, landscape, fit and tiled printing with snapshot/version labels.
Generate PDFs asynchronously from a consistent publication or explicitly labelled current-data snapshot.
Implement private authenticated expiring downloads and per-field export permissions.
Escape spreadsheet formula text; default public outputs to no email/private notes.
Restrict PDF asset loading to controlled local/static inputs and review actual rendered pages.
acceptance_criteria: PDFs and print pages have no clipped text or missing SVG furniture.
Unauthorized users cannot fetch artifacts by UUID/path.
Public documents omit private fields.
CSV export cells do not execute spreadsheet formulas.

tasks.title: Schedules, cleanup and recovery jobs
implementation_steps: Register periodic hold expiry, due-mail dispatch, abandoned-claim reconciliation and file/retention cleanup.
Store due times/progress in PostgreSQL; keep distant schedules out of Celery ETA queues.
Define idempotent task boundaries, time limits and actor/tenant rechecks.
Handle cancellation of events and revocation of user permissions between enqueue and execution.
Implement owner-reviewed data export/deletion with configurable retention and protected audit history.
acceptance_criteria: Stopping beat does not block reuse of expired holds.
Worker/broker failure can resume safe jobs without partial business commits.
Retention respects live events, policy settings and artifact access.

tasks.title: Production container and database hardening
implementation_steps: Separate runtime non-superuser DB credentials from migration-owner credentials using explicit secret mounts.
Create idempotent documented provisioning/grants; runtime cannot CREATE/DROP schema or bypass ownership.
Lock dependency versions and service image digests after integration testing.
Ensure non-root processes can write only intended private/static/beat/tmp paths; validate secret readability without printing secrets.
Verify proxy trust, HTTPS, security headers, CSRF, private files, health and worker checks.
Keep migrations/collectstatic in release job; document maintenance deployment and safe rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime DB role has only required permissions and migrations work with release role.
Fresh dev and production configurations validate.
Staging image builds, migration, HTTPS login and worker tests have recorded evidence.

tasks.title: Monitoring, backups and restore rehearsal
implementation_steps: Add structured redacted logs, request/job IDs and protected metrics endpoints.
Monitor error rate, latency, queue age, worker heartbeat, disk and backup freshness.
Provide encrypted off-host DB/private-file backup and retention scripts using dedicated credentials.
Document broker recovery/outbox reconciliation and provider outage response.
Restore into an isolated test environment with real-email sending disabled and verify seats/private files.
acceptance_criteria: Backups are usable, not just created.
Restore rehearsal records measured RPO/RTO and checks business state.
Secrets, email bodies and token URLs are absent from ordinary logs.

tasks.title: Full-system acceptance, accessibility and performance
implementation_steps: Run A01-A20 with evidence links, build identifiers and timestamps.
Exercise PostgreSQL concurrency with separate connections, tenant access and stale revisions.
Test timezone/DST edges, injection uploads, CSV limits and security failures.
Run keyboard/screen-reader and mobile workflows plus PDF visual review.
Benchmark 10000 tickets, 1000 tables and 20 staff users on documented hardware.
Fix regressions and rerun affected checks; distinguish targets from measured results.
acceptance_criteria: All mandatory acceptance cases pass or are explicitly release-blocked.
p95 page/API <500 ms, assignment <750 ms, import <60 s and initial usable layout <3 s on the reference workload, or reviewed corrective work remains open.
No known data-integrity or tenant-isolation failures remain.

tasks.title: Developer and operator handover
implementation_steps: Document exact startup, seed/demo, test, import, seating, publish, mail and print workflows.
Provide synthetic demo fixtures and accessible user walkthrough.
Document configuration, secret rotation, backups, rollback and remaining limitations.
Reconcile actual implementation with specification and mark only validated tasks complete.
acceptance_criteria: A new developer can run the complete local workflow from documented commands.
Final report names actual checks, blocked external checks and deployment prerequisites.
No required business workflow remains a stub.

validation_commands.notes: Run from project root. Commands assume T01 adds pytest dependencies; production commands require prepared secrets/config and an authorized target. These are validation instructions, not evidence they have run.
development: docker compose -f compose.dev.yaml exec web python manage.py check
docker compose -f compose.dev.yaml exec web python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
docker compose -f compose.dev.yaml exec web pytest
docker compose -f compose.dev.yaml exec worker celery -A config inspect ping
staging_only: docker compose --env-file .env.prod -f compose.prod.yaml run --rm web python manage.py check --deploy
additional_checks_to_implement: Browser suite with Playwright and documented browser runtime
Concurrency integration tests using real PostgreSQL transactions
PDF page rendering and visual inspection
MailDev assertions and separately authorized real SendGrid smoke test

definition_of_done: A01-A20 verified on staging; missing credentials or infrastructure produce explicit release blockers, never assumed passes.
Migrations and constraints committed; dependency locks and tested container images recorded.
UI workflows persist correctly and meet keyboard-accessibility requirements.
Production secrets, least-privilege roles, monitoring and restore procedures validated.
No real guest sends or live deployments occur without authorization.
suggested_cursor_prompt: Read CURSOR_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.json, SPECIFICATION.md and README.md. Inspect the supplied scaffold and implement the plan in dependency order, starting at the first incomplete task. Maintain IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.json with actual evidence. Build working end-to-end features and run relevant validation; continue independent work if an external check is blocked. Follow the plan's invariants, scope and authorization boundaries.
